title: Pairing from repulsive interactions in twisted WSe2 from functional renormalization
authors: Hannes Braun, Dumitru Călugăru, Pietro M. Bonetti, Haoyu Hu, Yan Zhang, Yi Jiang, Quansheng Wu, Kin Fai Mak, Jie Shan, B. Andrei Bernevig, Michael M. Scherer, Laura Classen
abstract: Motivated by the observation of superconductivity in twisted bilayer WSe$_2$ over an extended range of displacement fields, reaching from the correlated insulator down to zero field, we analyze the correlated electron phases of this system at hole filling $ν= -1$ and twist angle $3.65^\circ$ using Hartree--Fock, random phase approximation, and functional renormalization group calculations. We derive a continuum model with gate-screened Coulomb interaction from first principles and compare its instabilities to those of a realistic three-orbital Wannier model with a Hubbard interaction and an artificial single-orbital Hubbard model. In both cases, we find a superconducting instability of mixed $d$-wave singlet and $p$-wave triplet character, arising adjacent to inter-valley-coherent spin-density-wave order in the phase diagram spanned by displacement field and interaction strength. Our additional analysis of the pairing mechanism points to inter-valley coherent spin fluctuations as the pairing glue. The extent of the pairing regime and the associated critical temperatures depend on the model input, and we trace differences to the interaction range entering the projected interaction. Within the continuum model, the gate-screened Coulomb interaction yields pairing down to zero displacement field, bringing theory into agreement with experiment.
summary: This work theoretically analyzes superconductivity in twisted WSe2, finding that repulsive interactions drive the system into a mixed d-wave/p-wave superconducting state. The pairing mechanism is robustly attributed to inter-valley coherent spin fluctuations. By comparing continuum models with realistic Wannier models using FRG and RPA, the authors reconcile theory with experimental observations across varying strain fields.
main_problem: The study investigates the superconducting instability arising from repulsive interactions in twisted bilayer WSe2, aiming to identify the microscopic pairing mechanism.
main_result: The pairing instability is driven by inter-valley coherent spin fluctuations, leading to a mixed d-wave singlet and p-wave triplet superconducting state.
method: The analysis employs advanced theoretical techniques including Hartree-Fock, Random Phase Approximation (RPA), and Functional Renormalization Group (FRG) calculations.
model_or_system: The system is twisted bilayer WSe2, analyzed using continuum models derived from first principles and compared against realistic three-orbital Wannier models (e.g., 3Tri model).
key_observables: Superconducting critical temperature (Tc), pairing symmetry (d-wave/p-wave), and the nature of the pairing glue (spin fluctuations).
important_parameters: Hole filling $\nu = -1$, twist angle $3.65^\circ$, and the displacement field ($D$) which controls the phase diagram.
main_assumptions: The analysis often compares results from different interaction approximations (Hubbard vs. Coulomb) and relies on projecting RPA fluctuations onto the pairing channel.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the phase diagram showing coexisting SDW and superconducting regions, and plots detail the evolution of Tc and the structure of the leading pairing eigenfunction.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the phase diagram using multiple theoretical tools (HF, RPA, FRG) to map out competing ordered states (SDW vs. SC) and pin down the pairing mechanism by comparing results from different interaction models.
why_interesting: The detailed theoretical mapping of competing orders (SDW/SC) and the identification of spin fluctuations as the pairing glue provides a rich theoretical framework applicable to other correlated 2D van der Waals heterostructures.
